Do not judge hidden reasoning. Do not use tools, browse, execute code or delegate. Only explicit user requirements are mandatory; do not convert optional improvements into constraints. Fiction may invent facts if allowed by the request. Do not reward verbosity or decorative formatting. Do not invent factual errors.
Give four separate aspect scores completion, logic, value, clarity, each 0 to 5 in increments of 0.5. Anchors: 0=no effective content; 1=severe failure; 2=major gaps; 3=basically useful with meaningful weaknesses; 4=strong with limited weaknesses; 5=exceptional execution with no material weakness. Use half steps only between anchors. Do not force differences or a score distribution.
For each aspect give a brief Chinese reason and one short exact contiguous quotation from the candidate as evidence. Do not add ellipses, change spelling or paraphrase quotations. If relevant content is missing, evidence may be an empty string and reason must describe the missing content. List material errors in critical_errors, otherwise an empty list; needs_review=true when genuine uncertainty needs human checking. Give a brief Chinese overall reason. Return only schema-conforming JSON; aggregate is computed locally.

Confirm occupancy patterns and existing heating equipment. Obtain usable roof area, shading, orientation, structural capacity, local solar radiation, temperatures and freeze exposure. These inputs determine feasible collector capacity, storage volume and solar contribution; occupancy alone cannot establish sizes.\n\n2. **Select components and map connections.** Compare flat-plate and evacuated-tube collectors against climate, roof constraints and service availability. Plan insulated storage, circulation equipment, controls, expansion vessels, pressure/temperature relief, isolation valves and a thermostatic mixing valve for safe delivery. A typical arrangement is **collectors → heat-transfer loop → storage heat exchanger; potable cold water → solar storage → backup heater → mixing valve → building distribution**. Select direct, indirect antifreeze or drainback circulation only after confirming freeze risk, water quality and applicable codes. Account for distribution and recirculation heat losses.\n\n3. **Define seasonal and backup operation.** Use differential-temperature controls to collect heat when collectors are hotter than storage. Provide backup heating capable of meeting the required load during low sunshine, peak demand or solar-system outages. Choose the backup fuel and control strategy after obtaining existing equipment details, electrical capacity and energy tariffs. Establish climate-appropriate freeze protection and a summer overheating strategy, including low-occupancy conditions. Maintain hygienic storage and distribution temperatures under local requirements, with scald protection at delivery.\n\n4. **Review installation and maintenance risks.** Require structural assessment, approved roof anchoring, waterproof penetrations, wind/snow-load checks and safe maintenance access. Address hot surfaces, working at height, leaks, corrosion, scaling, electrical safety and compatibility between heat-transfer fluids and potable-water protection requirements. Route relief discharges safely and provide accessible isolation and drainage. Set a maintenance schedule for collector inspection, insulation, pumps, valves, sensors, fluid condition and any sacrificial anodes. Water chemistry and local service capability affect equipment selection and maintenance frequency.\n\n5. **Verify performance before committing and after commissioning.** Model feasible options using measured demand, local weather, actual roof constraints and distribution losses. Compare annual useful solar heat, backup energy, overheating risk and lifecycle cost; obtain installed quotations and energy prices before estimating savings or payback. At commissioning, verify flow, sensor readings, controls, leak tightness, mixing temperatures and safety devices. Meter hot-water consumption, useful solar heat and backup energy, then compare weather- and occupancy-adjusted results with predictions across seasons. Investigate shortfalls before expanding or resizing the system."}
